[0] When Apple finally responded to soaring memory and other component costs, it didn't hold back. Some increases were over fifty percent, and pricing on some memory and storage upgrade options even doubled.

[1] These higher prices are likely to persist for years — and may never come back down……

[2] 9to5Mac readers have long questioned whether Apple would reduce prices once component supply pressures eased. Over two-thirds of readers said they expected this price hike to be permanent.

[3] A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing wouldn't improve until 2028, and even when it did, the improvement would be very modest. The currently elevated prices remaining high for years to come — and likely never returning to previous levels — is now a foregone conclusion.

[4] If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same pace? Or would you reduce the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Alternatively, would you take other measures, such as buying cheaper models, opting for refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?

[5] Feel free to take part in our poll, and share your thoughts in the comments section. The poll supports multiple selections, and you can plan to change your purchasing behavior in multiple ways.
